site.name: Sallie Barber Mine
site.componentDetail: Historic underground zinc-lead-silver mine with stabilized headframe, ore bin, shaft interpretation, and surface equipment
overview: The Sallie Barber Mine is a preserved historic mine site east of Breckenridge in the French Gulch area. The mine opened in the 1880s and was worked intermittently into the 1940s.

The site is especially useful for understanding underground mine operations because surviving and restored surface features interpret the shaft, headframe, ore handling, hoisting, compressed-air drilling, and related equipment.

timeline.text: The Sallie Barber Mine opened during the expansion of hard-rock mining east of Breckenridge.
The mine shipped zinc-rich ore during a period when zinc became an increasingly important commodity in the Breckenridge district.
After an earlier shutdown, the mine reopened as wartime demand increased the value of zinc.
Intermittent operation ended and the Sallie Barber ultimately closed.
Breckenridge History, Summit County, and the Town of Breckenridge stabilized the mine site, reinforced the ore bin, and restored artifacts.
Interpretive improvements documented the mine's underground layout and the function of surviving and reconstructed surface equipment.

moreHistory: Breckenridge History describes the underground mine as having three levels and a sump extending to about 365 feet. Interpretation at the site explains how a steam plant and steam hoist powered ore buckets through the headframe.
Ore brought to the surface could be directed to the ore bin or moved by ore car to the hillside waste dump. Surviving interpretation also includes a belt-driven air compressor and a rock drill.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 75 describes the Sallie Barber vein and its zinc-rich mineralization, including sphalerite and pyrite in a mineralized fissure zone.
